newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Parliament urges sanctions against Burma.
newsitem.headline: Euro Parliament urges sanctions against Burma.

text.p: The European Parliament called on Wednesday for economic sanctions against Burma because of human rights abuses in the Southeast Asian country.

It urged European Union foreign ministers at their meeting in Luxembourg on October 28-29 to respond to a request from Burmese opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner, Aung San Suu Kyi, to end all trade, tourism and investment links with the country.
In a resolution, the parliament strongly condemned Burma's military government for "violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms being perpetrated against the Burmese people".
It noted the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) had recently detained more than 800 opposition members and that over 80,000 people had been forced to quit their homes by the army.
Kyi Maung, deputy chairman of Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD), was detained for questioning by the SLORC on Tuesday, diplomats and party sources said.

The European Commission is completing an inquiry into possible future suspension of trade benefits, worth tens of millions of dollars annually, available to Burma under the generalised system of preferences.
The EU's Irish presidency said earlier this month the 15-nation bloc was considering curbs against Burma.
